grades.why: It describes --latest as using the latest Worker runtime version and claims it is a legacy option with little effect, instead of saying it sets the compatibility date to the newest date the bundled workerd supports.

It presents the stale behavior (just remove `nodejs_compat` to disable) as the main fix and only vaguely hints at a `no_` flag, never stating that both `no_nodejs_compat` and `no_nodejs_compat_v2` must be set.
It presents `--legacy-env` and `legacy_env = false` service environments as usable options, mentioning only a vague deprecation, instead of stating they are removed and the field now errors.
It omits `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and gives only the stale `WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false`/`wrangler telemetry disable` approach.
It states the stale claim that D1 only supports eu and fedramp jurisdictions with no US option, instead of `--jurisdiction us`.
It claims logs only go to the terminal and observability doesn't apply locally, omitting the default Local Explorer Observability capture and the X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=false opt-out.
It affirms the stale 3 MB/10 MB compressed limits as current, contradicting the key's single 64 MiB uncompressed limit with no compressed limit.
It presents the stale `wrangler r2 sql` path and the no-longer-read `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` as current instead of `wrangler basin sql` with `WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN`.
It says DOs are updated to new code immediately with no built-in way to defer, missing the code update strategy option (immediate/deferred, default deferred 5 min), which matches the stale behavior.
It says Workers cannot accept inbound raw TCP at all. That is the stale answer; it omits the experimental local-dev `connect` config entry and the `connect(socket, env, ctx)` handler.
It states the stale behavior that Workflows have no per-workflow concurrency setting and only account limits apply, never mentioning `workflows[].concurrency.limit`.
It calls provisioning beta and says Queues are not auto-created, contradicting the key that it is GA and covers Queue bindings.
It gives the stale `/cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled` path as current instead of `/cdn-cgi/local/*` from Miniflare v5.
It leaves the alpha status open and presents the stale CPU-profile behavior as current, never mentioning bundle sizes and only hedging on a summary.
It claims bulk can only create or update secrets and says to delete with `wrangler versions secret delete`, which is the stale behavior, instead of setting the key to null in the JSON.
The answer says it doesn't know of a Channels export and suggests checking, without stating the agents/experimental/channels path.
It says yes, unique-ID stubs can be called over RPC with only possible name-related misbehavior, rather than stating that the first async RPC fails and Agents must be addressed by name.
The answer only issues tool calls to search the workspace and never addresses which transports useAgent supports.
It hedges that it isn't aware of an official terminal client and offers workarounds, never mentioning `npx agents tui <url>` or flatly claiming none exists.
It says getCurrentAgent() inside queued callbacks returns the agent but not the original connection or request, which matches the key.
It says Agent still extends PartyServer's Server, which is the stale answer; the hedge doesn't undo that claim.
The answer says it can't confirm subAgent()'s status and only gives conditional advice, without stating that it is deprecated in favor of this.dynamicAgents.
It says the second argument is the `Schedule` object, and it never describes it as a raw row with a JSON-string payload.

It says scheduling is only available via `this.schedule()` on an Agent subclass, which is the stale behavior, and it never mentions the `Scheduler` capability exported from `agents/schedules` that any Durable Object can use.
The answer only issues a search tool call and never addresses the question or states any fact about wrapAISDK or createAISDKTelemetry.
The answer only contains tool calls searching for source files and never addresses how to construct MCPClientManager.
It says the client first sends `initialize`, which is the stale behavior, and never mentions probing with `server/discover` first.
It presents the stale claim that createMcpHandler is built around a v1 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk McpServer as current, and never says it accepts a v2 server factory.
The answer only shows an intent to run a command and never states whether agents supports AI SDK v7.
It says the test can still pass and newer versions only add a warning, contradicting the key that un-awaited async assertions now fail the test.
It states Vitest does not walk up to parent directories and only looks in the current root, matching the key, without presenting the stale ancestor-search behavior as current.
It claims toHaveTextContent does substring matching, which is the stale behavior; per the key it now matches strictly and toMatchTextContent is used for partial matching.

It gives the stale usage of @vitest/browser-webdriverio as a core provider and never mentions that it moved to community maintenance in the vitest-community organization or that version 5.0.0 works with Vitest 5.

It recommends adding @vitest/runner as a dependency pinned in lockstep with vitest, presenting the stale separate-package approach as current instead of noting it is deprecated and that runner APIs come from `vitest`.
It states the stale default .vitest-reports/ instead of the current .vitest/blob/ directory.
It claims locators match substrings by default, which is the stale behavior; the key says exact matching is the default.
It says describe and test names are joined by spaces, which is the stale behavior; the key says they are joined with `>`.
It states the stale behavior that inline projects don't inherit the root config unless `extends: true` is set, contradicting the key that inheritance is the default.
It states that the poll rejects and the test fails when the timeout elapses while the callback is still pending, which matches the key and does not present the stale behavior.
It claims Vitest has no built-in when()-style API and recommends mockImplementation, matching the stale answer instead of mentioning Vitest 5's vi.when().
It says Vitest only warns and still hoists vi.mock outside the top level, which is the stale behavior; the key says it now throws an error.
It identifies the `--repeats` CLI option for rerunning tests and only mentions the per-test option as an additional or fallback choice, not as the only way.
It states the stale claim that --project has no short flag, contradicting the key that -p is the shorthand.
It says vitest list loads/executes test files to collect tests, which is the stale behavior; the key says it parses files statically by default.
The answer consists only of repeated tool calls and never states whether useAgentChat throttles or renders every chunk.
